rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خصيم means someone who argues in a dispute.
rows.anchor: الخصيم المحتج في الخصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مبين describes someone who clearly expresses what is within him.
rows.anchor: والمبين هو المفصح عما في ضميره

words: خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast displays God's power in bringing a human from a lowly drop to eloquence and capability.
rows.anchor: إخراجه من النطفة المهينة إلى أن صار بهذه الحال في البيان والمكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description should make people recognize God's favor in bringing them from a lowly drop to their present state.
rows.anchor: ليعرفه نعم الله تعالى عليه في إخراجه إلى هذه الحال بعدما خلقه من نطفة مهينة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The description exposes the gross ingratitude of wasting God's favor by disputing in disbelief.
rows.anchor: فاحش ما ارتكب من تضييع النعمة بالخصومة في الكفر , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who scattered decayed bones and challenged the possibility of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وذكر الكلبي أن هذه الآية نزلت في أبي بن خلف الجمحي حين أخذ عظاما نخرة فذراها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thing Moses came to was the fire, which was light.
rows.anchor: يعني النار , التي هو نور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view is that God addressed Moses directly and alone.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا النداء قولان : أحدهما : أنه تفرد بندائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God made the light speak with a call from His inseparable light, calming Moses so he could bear God's command.
rows.anchor: أن الله أنطق النور بهذا النداء فكان من نوره الذي لا ينفصل عنه

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، الحسن، ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ali, al-Hasan, and Ibn Jurayj say Moses was told to remove his shoes so his feet would touch the holy valley's blessing.
rows.anchor: ليباشر بقدميه بركة الوادي المقدس , قاله علي بن أبي طالب ، والحسن ، وابن جريج

rows.speaker: كعب، عكرمة، قتادة
rows.claim: Kaʿb, ʿIkrima, and Qatada say the shoes were made from the hide of a dead donkey.
rows.anchor: لأن نعليه كانتا من جلد حمار ميت , قاله كعب , وعكرمة , وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid interpret المقدس as blessed.
rows.anchor: أن المقدس هو المبارك , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub interprets المقدس as purified.
rows.anchor: أنه المطهر , قاله قطرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas derives Ṭuwā from traversing the valley at night and thereby folding or crossing it.
rows.anchor: أنه اسم من طوى لأنه مر بواديها ليلا فطواه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation derives Ṭuwā from two calls: Arabic طوى can mean twice, as the second call overlays the first.
rows.anchor: سمي طوى لأن الله تعالى ناداه مرتين . وطوى في كلامهم بمعنى مرتين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the valley was named Ṭuwā because it was sanctified twice.
rows.anchor: بل سمي بذلك لأن الوادي قدس مرتين , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets Ṭuwā as an instruction to tread the valley with one's foot.
rows.anchor: أن معنى طوى : طإ الوادي بقدمك , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Ṭuwā was the valley's ancient proper name.
rows.anchor: أنه الاسم للوادي قديما , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets establishing prayer for God's remembrance as remembering Him during prayer.
rows.anchor: وأقم الصلاة لتذكرني فيها , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to establish prayer by remembering God, since one enters prayer only through His remembrance.
rows.anchor: وأقم الصلاة بذكري , لأنه لا يدخل في الصلاة إلا بذكره

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim interprets the phrase as praying when one remembers the prayer.
rows.anchor: وأقم الصلاة حين تذكرها , قاله إبراهيم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib reports that the Prophet said whoever forgets a prayer should perform it when he remembers.
rows.anchor: وروى سعيد بن المسيب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها )

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God nearly conceals the Hour from everyone; here أكاد means “I intend.”
rows.anchor: أي لا أظهر عليها أحدا , قاله الحسن , ويكون أكاد بمعنى أريد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid read the phrase as hiding the Hour from Himself, to stress how inaccessible its knowledge is; Ubayy's reading adds “from myself.”
rows.anchor: أكاد أخفيها من نفسي , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد , وهي كذلك في قراة أبي

rows.speaker: الأنباري
rows.claim: Al-Anbari pauses after أكاد, supplies “I nearly bring it,” then restarts with أخفيها, conveying the Hour's nearness before saying it is hidden.
rows.anchor: انقطع الكلام عند أكاد وبعده مضمر أكاد آتي بها تقريبا لورودها , ثم استأنف : أخفيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes اصطنعتك as “I created you,” deriving it from صنع.
rows.anchor: خلقتك , مأخوذ من الصنعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes اصطنعتك as “I chose you,” deriving it from الصنيعة.
rows.anchor: اخترتك , مأخوذ من الصنيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For Myself” may mean for My love.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : لمحبتي . الثاني : لرسالتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “For Myself” may instead mean for My message.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : لمحبتي . الثاني : لرسالتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is “do not slacken in remembering Me”; the cited line about Muhammad's steadfastness illustrates ونى.
rows.anchor: لا تفترا في ذكري , قال الشاعر : فما ونى محمد مذ أن غفر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the command as “do not grow weak in My mission.”
rows.anchor: لا تضعفا في رسالتي , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the command as “do not delay.”
rows.anchor: لا تبطنا , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبان
rows.claim: Aban interprets it as “do not cease” and cites a line by Ṭarafa describing pots that never stop boiling.
rows.anchor: لا تزالا , حكاه أبان واستشهد بقول طرفة : كأن القدور الراسيات أمامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the brothers should address Pharaoh gently and softly.
rows.anchor: لطيفا رقيقا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says they were to address Pharaoh by his kunya.
rows.anchor: كنياه , قاله السدي وقيل إن كنية فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported kunyas of Pharaoh are Abu Murra and Abu al-Walid.
rows.anchor: كنية فرعون أبو مرة , وقيل أبو الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is to begin with enticement before warning, softening Pharaoh before confronting him with threat.
rows.anchor: أن يبدأه بالرغبة قبل الرهبة , ليلين بها فيتوطأ بعدها من رهبة ووعيد

rows.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
rows.claim: Some Sufis marvel that God treats an enemy with such gentleness and ask how gentle He must be to one who supports Him.
rows.anchor: يا رب هذا رفقك لمن عاداك , فكيف رفقك بمن والاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said Pharaoh had treated Moses well while raising him, so gentleness repaid that kindness when Moses could not repay him otherwise.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن فرعون كان يحسن لموسى حين رباه , فأراد أن يجعل رفقه به مكافأة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that Pharaoh might hurry against them; a rajaz line glosses the verb with hastening.
rows.anchor: أن يعجل علينا , قال الراجز : قد أفرط العلج علينا وعجل

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains it as punishing them like someone excessive in sin; in usage, الإفراط is excess and التفريط is shortcoming.
rows.anchor: يعذبنا عذاب الفارط في الذنب , وهو المتقدم فيه , قاله المبرد ويقال لمن أكثر في الشيء أفرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feared transgression is that Pharaoh might kill them.
rows.anchor: أو أن يطغى } أي يقتلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although throwing magic is unbelief and cannot properly be commanded, the command may function as a conditional statement: if you regard your act as proof, then throw.
rows.anchor: اللفظ على صفة الأمر , ومعناه معنى الخبر , وتقديره : إن كان إلقاؤكم عندكم حجة فألقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses asked them to throw as a test that would manifest his prophethood and show that what defeated their magic was not magic.
rows.anchor: على وجه الاعتبار ليظهر لهم صحة نبوته ووضوح محبته , وأن ما أبطل السحر لم يكن سحرا

rows.speaker: القاسم بن أبي بزة
rows.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bizza is reported to say that the sorcerers numbered seventy thousand.
rows.anchor: فحكي عن القاسم بن أبي بزة أنهم كانوا سبعين ألف ساحر

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj is reported to count nine hundred sorcerers: three hundred from al-ʿArish, three hundred from al-Fayyum, and perhaps three hundred from Alexandria.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن ابن جريج أنهم كانوا تسعمائة ساحر , ثلاثمائة من العريش , وثلاثمائة من الفيوم

rows.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that there were seventy-two sorcerers, two Copts and seventy Israelites, who began the day as sorcerers and ended it as martyrs.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس أنهم كانوا اثنين وسبعين ساحرا , منهم اثنان من القبط وسبعون من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “it seemed to him” may refer to Pharaoh or to Moses.
rows.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : أنه يخيل ذلك لفرعون . الثاني : لموسى كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses may have feared that people would confuse the sorcerers' feat with his and think his act was the same kind of magic.
rows.anchor: أن يلتبس على الناس أمرهم فيتوهموا أنهم فعلوا مثل فعله وأنه من جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that he felt the natural caution built into human dispositions.
rows.anchor: لما هو مركوز في الطباع من الحذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أوجس means to keep or conceal something within oneself.
rows.anchor: وأوجس : بمعنى أسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reassurance steadied Moses and removed his fear.
rows.anchor: تثبيتا لنفسه , وإزالة لخوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff was to take their work into its mouth and swallow it quickly.
rows.anchor: أي تأخذه بفيها ابتلاعا بسرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said the staff swallowed a load of ropes and staffs carried by three hundred camels; Moses then took it and it returned to its former shape.
rows.anchor: فقيل إنها ابتلعت حمل ثلاثمائة بعير من الحبال والعصي , ثم أخذها موسى ورجعت عصا كما كانت

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Moses' staff was made from an ʿawsaj thorn tree.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت من عوسج , قاله وهب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the staff came from Paradise and that Moses killed ʿUj ibn ʿAnaq with it.
rows.anchor: من الجنة , قاله ابن عباس , قال : وبها قتل موسى عوج بن عناق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers prostrated in obedience to God and affirmation of Moses.
rows.anchor: طاعة لله وتصديقا لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They meant the Lord whom Aaron and Moses called them to worship, who is Lord of them and all creation.
rows.anchor: أي بالرب الذي دعا إليه هارون وموسى , لأنه رب لنا ولجميع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the sorcerers did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise and the reward of its people.
rows.anchor: فقيل إنهم , ما رفعوا رؤوسهم حتى رأوا الجنة وثواب أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their straying refers to worship of the calf.
rows.anchor: يعني بعبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that Aaron should have followed Moses by leaving rather than staying with those who strayed.
rows.anchor: ألا تتبعني في الخروج ولا تقم مع من ضل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid's cited view is that Aaron should have followed Moses' practice of restraining and rebuking them.
rows.anchor: ألا تتبع عادتي في منعهم والإنكار عليهم , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had ordered Aaron to succeed him and set matters right; because Aaron stayed and did not firmly stop or condemn the calf worship, Moses accused him of disobedience.
rows.anchor: أخلفني في قومي وأصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين فلما أقام معهم ولم يبالغ في منعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view is that Moses and Aaron were full brothers.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان أخاه لأبيه وأمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that they shared a father but not a mother; Aaron said “son of my mother” to soften and appeal to Moses.
rows.anchor: أنه كان أخاه لأبيه دون أمه , وإنما قال يا ابن أم ترفيقا له واستعطافا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Moses seized Aaron's hair with his right hand and his beard with his left.
rows.anchor: أنه أخذ شعره بيمينه , ولحيته بيسراه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Moses took Aaron by the ear and beard, with “head” standing for ear among those who count the ear as part of the head.
rows.anchor: أنه أخذ بأذنه ولحيته , فعبر عن الأذن بالرأس , وهو قول من جعل الأذن من الرأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed reason for Moses seizing Aaron is that Moses wanted to whisper about the Tablets' descent and conceal them from Israel before repentance; Aaron asked him not to confuse his secret.
rows.anchor: ليسر إليه نزول الألواح عليه , لأنها نزلت عليه في هذه المناجاة . وأراد أن يخفيها عن بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second proposed reason is that Moses thought Aaron sided with Israel over the calf, but the author says such a thought is impermissible for prophets.
rows.anchor: الثاني : فعل ذلك لأنه وقع في نفسه أن هارون مائل إلى بني إسرئيل فيما فعلوه من أمر العجل , ومثل هذا لا يجوز على الأنبياء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeliest reason is that Moses seized Aaron for refraining from condemning the calf worshipers and remaining among their sins.
rows.anchor: الثالث : وهو الأشبه - أنه فعل ذلك لإمساكه عن الإنكار على بني إسرئيل الذين عبدوا العجل ومقامه بينهم على معاصيهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron's answer may mean that Moses divided Israel through disagreement in their beliefs.
rows.anchor: فرقت بينهم بما وقع من اختلاف معتقدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Moses would have divided them by fighting those who worshiped the calf.
rows.anchor: الثاني : [ فرقت ] بينهم بقتال من عبد العجل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains it as “you did not act according to my instruction.”
rows.anchor: لم تعمل بوصيتي , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains it as “you did not wait for my instruction.”
rows.anchor: لم تنتظر عهدي , قاله أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says all Israel worshiped the calf except twelve thousand who remained with Aaron.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنهم عبدوه جميعا إلا اثني عشر ألفا بقوا مع هارون لم يعبدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Extending one's eyes means looking.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد بمد العين النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes extending the eyes as grief or regret.
rows.anchor: أراد به الأسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أزواجا means kinds or categories, from the idea of pairing.
rows.anchor: أي أشكالا , مأخوذ من المزاوجة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the world's زهرة as its adornment.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : زينة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets the trial as punishing them through the worldly adornment they were given.
rows.anchor: لنفتنهم أي لنعذبهم به , قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is that worldly gifts turn them away from their interests.
rows.anchor: لنميلهم عن مصالحهم وهو محتمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is contentment with what one possesses and renunciation of what one does not possess.
rows.anchor: أنه القناعة بما يملكه والزهد فيما لا يملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God's afterlife reward is better and more lasting than the worldly provision given to others.
rows.anchor: وثواب ربك في الآخرة خير وأبقى مما متعنا به هؤلاء في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that lawful provision that remains is better than abundant provision that leads to transgression.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الحلال المبقي خيرا من الكثير المطغي

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafiʿ reports that the verse was revealed after a Jewish lender demanded collateral for food borrowed by the Prophet, who grieved and offered his armor.
rows.anchor: ما رواه أبو رافع أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استلف من يهودي طعاما فأبى أن يسلفه إلا برهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after this verse was revealed, the Prophet had a caller announce that neglecting God's discipline leaves the soul cut by regret for worldly life.
rows.anchor: وروى أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مناديه فنادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your family” may mean the Prophet's relatives by lineage.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد أهله المناسبين له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean everyone who followed and believed in him, since obedience makes them like his family.
rows.anchor: جميع من اتبعه وآمن به , لأنهم يحلون بالطاعة له محل أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to persevere in performing prayer and in enjoining it on one's family.
rows.anchor: اصبر على فعلها وعلى أمرهم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though addressed to the Prophet, the assurance applies to all creatures: God provides for them without needing provision and benefits them without receiving benefit, emphasizing His favor.
rows.anchor: فالمراد به جميع الخلق أنه تعالى يرزقهم ولا يسترزقهم , وينفعهم ولا ينتفع بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good outcome belongs to the people of piety.
rows.anchor: أي وحسن العاقبة لأهل التقوى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the time of punishment for Mecca's people had drawn near; they had dismissed the promised punishment as delayed, and they were killed at Badr.
rows.anchor: قرب وقت عذابهم , يعني أهل مكة , لأنهم استبطؤوا ما وعدوا به من العذاب تكذيبا , فكان قتلهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the nearness as the approaching time of reckoning at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قرب وقت حسابهم وهو قيام الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning is near because whatever must come will come, and everything that comes is near.
rows.anchor: لا بد آت , وكل آت قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also be called near because much time has elapsed and little remains.
rows.anchor: لأن الزمان لكثرة ما مضى وقلة ما بقي قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that they are heedless through worldly preoccupation and turn away from the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: في غفلة بالدنيا معرضون عن الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are heedless through error and turn away from guidance.
rows.anchor: في غفلة بالضلال , معرضون عن الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remembrance is newly recited as revelation descends a surah after a surah and a verse after a verse over time.
rows.anchor: التنزيل مبتدأ التلاوة لنزوله سورة بعد سورة . وآية بعد آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They listen to the revelation but then refuse to accept it.
rows.anchor: أي استمعوا تنزيله فتركوا قبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may mean that they amuse themselves or that they occupy themselves.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : أي يلهون . الثاني : يشتغلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means amusement, they may be absorbed in pleasures or in listening to what is recited to them.
rows.anchor: بلذاتهم . الثاني : بسماع ما يتلى عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means occupation, they may be busy with worldly life, which is play and diversion, or with criticizing and objecting to revelation.
rows.anchor: بالدنيا , لأنها لعب كما قال تعالى : ^ { إنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو } ^ [ الحديد : 20 ]

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says that whenever revelation was renewed for them, they persisted in ignorance.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : كلما جدد لهم الذكر استمروا على الجهل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says their hearts are distracted from remembrance by amusement.
rows.anchor: يعني غافله باللهو عن الذكر , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Ibn Shajara says their hearts are occupied with falsehood instead of truth.
rows.anchor: مشغلة بالباطل عن الحق , قاله ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation from dust refers to Adam.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descendants of Adam are meant by the drop of semen.
rows.anchor: يعني ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drop becomes a clinging clot in the womb.
rows.anchor: يعني أن النطفة تصير في الرحم علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A مضغة is the mass of flesh about the size of what can be chewed; the clot becomes that mass.
rows.anchor: يعني أن العلقة تصير مضغة , وذلك مقدار ما يمضع من اللحم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the formed is what becomes a creature, while the unformed is what the womb expels before the seed becomes formed.
rows.anchor: ما صار خلقا , وغير مخلقة ما دفعته الأرحام من النطف فلم يصير خلقا , وهو قول ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the pair as complete and incomplete in formation.
rows.anchor: معناه تامة الخلق وغير تامة الخلق , وهذا قول قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets them as shaped and unshaped, such as a miscarried fetus.
rows.anchor: معناه مصورة وغير مصورة كالسقط , وهذا قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets them as reaching full term or not reaching full term.
rows.anchor: يعني التام في شهوره , وغير التام , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran explains the beginning of human creation and the successive stages through which people pass.
rows.anchor: يعني في القرآن بدء خلقكم وتنقل أحوالكم

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the appointed term is completion.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : إلى التمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die before reaching decrepit old age.
rows.anchor: يعني قبل أن تبلغ إلى أرذل العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, some die before reaching full adulthood.
rows.anchor: قبل بلوغ الأشد

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam interprets the most decrepit age as old age.
rows.anchor: الهرم , وهو قول يحيى بن سلام

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says it is a return to a state like that at birth from the mother's womb.
rows.anchor: إلى مثل حاله عند خروجه من بطن أمه , حكاه النقاش

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: اليزيدي
rows.claim: Al-Yazidi interprets it as loss of intellect.
rows.anchor: ذهاب العقل , قاله اليزيدي

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that an elderly person can no longer acquire knowledge of things he once knew.
rows.anchor: لا يستفيد علما ما كان به عالما

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he no longer understands anything after having possessed reason.
rows.anchor: لا يعقل بعد عقله الأول شيئا

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that it may mean he can no longer act after knowing, since old age affects action more than knowledge and action depends on knowledge.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل عندي وجها ثالثا : أنه لا يعمل بعد علمه شيئا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says هامدة means dusty or gray.
rows.anchor: غبراء , وهذا قول قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it means dry and unable to grow anything.
rows.anchor: يابسة لا تنبت شيئا , وهذا قول ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation takes هامدة as worn-out or barren, citing al-Aʿsha's line about clothes that are faded and worn.
rows.anchor: أنها الدراسة , والهمود : الدروس , ومنه قول الأعشى : قالت قتيلة ما لجسمك شاحبا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets اهتزت as “grew.”
rows.anchor: معناه أنبتت , وهو قول الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plants themselves sway, with their movement becoming vigorous; a poem compares it to a branch in green leaves.
rows.anchor: معناه اهتز نباتها واهتزازه شدة حركته , كما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the earth increases or multiplies its growth.
rows.anchor: معناه أضعف نباتها

rows.speaker: الحسن، أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu ʿUbayda say the earth swells as plants emerge; on this reading, “swelled” precedes “stirred” in meaning, while the first reading needs no inversion.
rows.anchor: معناه انتفخت لظهور نباتها , فعلى هذا الوجه يكون مقدما ومؤخرا وتقديره : فإذا أنزلنا عليها الماء ربت واهتزت , وهذا قول الحسن وأبي عبيدة

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة
rows.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets each زوج as each kind or species.
rows.anchor: يعني من كل نوع , وهو قول ابن شجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is every color, since plants vary in green, red, and yellow.
rows.anchor: من كل لون لاختلاف ألوان النبات بالخضرة والحمرة والصفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بهيج means beautiful in appearance.
rows.anchor: يعني حسن الصورة

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam says that whoever God disgraces by sending to Hell has no one to honor him by admitting him to Paradise.
rows.anchor: ومن يهن الله فيدخله النار فما له من مكرم فيدخله الجنة

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: On Yahya ibn Sallam's reading, God does what He wills in reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: من ثواب وعقاب , وهذا قول يحيى بن سلام

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: الفراء، علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ and ʿAli ibn ʿIsa interpret God's disgrace as wretchedness and the absent honor as the absence of blessedness.
rows.anchor: ومن يهن الله بالشّقوة فما له من مكرم بالسعادة

rows.speaker: الفراء، علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: On their reading, God does what He wills in assigning wretchedness.
rows.anchor: من شقوة , وهذا قول الفراء وعلي بن عيسى

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that God may disgrace through vengeance, with no one to honor through beneficence.
rows.anchor: ومن يهن الله بالإنتقام فما له من مكرم بالإنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the author's added reading, God does as He wills in beneficence and vengeance.
rows.anchor: إن الله يفعل ما يشاء من إنعام وانتقام

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God repels disbelievers through believers, the disobedient through the obedient, and the ignorant through scholars.
rows.anchor: بالكفار عن المؤمنين , وبالعصاة عن المطيعين , وبالجهال عن العلماء

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُدَٰفِعُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟
rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah says God repels the darkness of innovation by the light of the Sunna.
rows.anchor: يدفع بنور السنة ظلمات البدعة , قاله سهل بن عبد الله

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj interprets the mutual repelling as God repelling polytheists through Muslims.
rows.anchor: ولولا دفع الله المشركين بالمسلمين , وهذا قول ابن جريج

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God protects religion through those who strive in His cause.
rows.anchor: ولولا دفع الله عن الدين بالمجاهدين , وهذا قول ابن زيد

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God protects believers through the prophets.
rows.anchor: ولولا دفع الله بالنبيين عن المؤمنين , وهذا قول الكلبي

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib says the Companions protected later generations of Successors through God's repelling.
rows.anchor: ولولا دفع الله بأصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عمن بعدهم من التابعين

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets it as God repelling harm through witnesses' testimony concerning rights.
rows.anchor: ولولا دفع الله بشهادة الشهود على الحقوق , وهذا قول مجاهد

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub says God protects people from harm through virtues.
rows.anchor: ولولا دفع الله على النفوس بالفضائل , وهذا قول قطرب

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds that God repels evil through good.
rows.anchor: ولولا دفع الله عن المنكر بالمعروف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the ṣawāmiʿ are monks' hermitages.
rows.anchor: أنها صوامع الرهبان , وهذا قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the ṣawāmiʿ are the places of prayer of the Sabeans.
rows.anchor: أنها مصلى الصابئين , وهو قول قتادة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says, “The believer's monastery is his house.”
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( صومعة المؤمن بيته )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is named for the narrowing together of its two sides; المنصمع means joined or contracted, as in أذن صمعاء.
rows.anchor: وسميت صومعة لانضمام طرفيها , والمنصمع : المنضم , ومنه أذن صمعاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the biyaʿ are Christian churches.
rows.anchor: أنها بيع النصارى , وهو قول قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the biyaʿ are Jewish synagogues.
rows.anchor: أنها كنائس اليهود , وهو قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بيعة is a foreign word adapted into Arabic.
rows.anchor: والبيعة اسم أعجمي معرب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the ṣalawāt are Jewish synagogues, which Jews call ṣalotā; the Arabic plural was adapted from that name.
rows.anchor: أنها كنائس اليهود يسمونها : صلوتا , فعرب جمعها , فقيل صلوات , وهذا قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn ʿIsa says ṣalawāt means prayers that were abandoned.
rows.anchor: معناه : وتركت صلوات , ذكره ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masājid are the mosques of Muslims.
rows.anchor: مساجد } المسلمين , ثم فيه قولان

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says polytheists would demolish the mosques in the present era if God did not repel them through Muslims.
rows.anchor: لهدمها الآن المشركون لولا دفع الله بالمسلمين , وهو معنى قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj assigns hermitages to Moses' law, churches to Jesus' law, and mosques to Muhammad's law; the verse thus means every place where God is worshiped in each dispensation.
rows.anchor: لهدمت صوامع في أيام شريعة موسى , وبيع في أيام شريعة عيسى ومساجد في أيام شريعة محمد
